patch.value:
## Problem

pm-a22j (closed) built scripts/measure-agent-token-surface.mjs: it measures the
full agent-facing token surface — root help, every per-command help, the
contracts payload family, and the MCP tools/list payload — and emits JSON so a
ratchet can diff it. pm-ksca (closed) then added a covering spec for it.

The harness is wired into nothing. Repository-wide search for
`measure-agent-token-surface` outside the script itself returns exactly one
hit, a historical CHANGELOG line. It has no package.json script, no CI step,
and no recorded baseline to diff against. Its own header comment tells the
reader to "re-run after each consolidation slice lands and diff against the
recorded baseline" — a baseline that is not stored anywhere in the repo.

## Consequence, measured 2026-07-26 on the live workspace

Nothing detects token-surface regressions, and they are present:

| command | output | approx tokens |
|---|---|---|
| pm graph audit --summary | 1,534 B | ~383 |
| pm list-open --limit 20 | 4,556 B | ~1,139 |
| pm get pm-96h7 | 5,365 B | ~1,341 |
| pm context --limit 10 | 6,195 B | ~1,548 |
| pm next --limit 5 | 8,799 B | ~2,199 |
| pm validate | 22,719 B | ~5,679 |
| **pm health --check-only** | **132,585 B** | **~33,146** |

`pm health --check-only` is the diagnostic AGENTS.md "When Unsure" routes
agents to, and a single invocation costs roughly a sixth of a 200k context
window. That specific regression is owned by pm-du93sr and `graph impact` by
pm-mfy1ux — this item owns the reason such regressions land and persist
undetected: the instrument that would have caught them on the commit that
introduced them runs nowhere.

## Why this is a child of pm-5t33or, not a duplicate

pm-5t33or owns the forward design: every command declares a default output
ceiling in its contract and degrades deterministically when it would exceed it.
That is the destination. This item is the enabling tranche that can ship
independently and immediately: take the harness that already exists and already
has a spec, record a committed baseline, and fail CI when the surface grows
beyond it. It requires no contract changes and no command behaviour changes,
and it makes pm-5t33or's rollout measurable slice by slice instead of
retrospective.

## Direction (not a mandate for the fix)

Add a package.json script, commit a baseline JSON artifact next to the
sdk-surface-snapshot baseline that already follows this pattern, and add a
static CI gate that diffs current against baseline with an allowed-growth
threshold and a documented update path. The sdk-surface-snapshot gate is the
working precedent for exactly this shape.
The agent token-surface harness from pm-a22j is wired into nothing, so output-size regressions like the 33k-token health check land undetected

scripts/measure-agent-token-surface.mjs measures root help, per-command help, contracts payloads and MCP tools/list, and has a covering spec, but has no package.json script, no CI step and no committed baseline. Repo-wide search finds one reference outside the file itself, a historical CHANGELOG line.

A package.json script runs the token-surface harness and a committed baseline artifact records the current surface; A static CI gate diffs measured against baseline and fails when growth exceeds the declared threshold, with a documented baseline-update path; The gate reproduces the currently measured values for health, validate, context, next, get and list-open so the baseline is verifiable
Turns an already-built, already-tested measurement into a continuous ratchet, so token regressions are caught at authoring time instead of during a manual audit.
Every agent-facing payload can grow without limit today; token cost is the scarcest resource in the agent loop.
A committed token-surface baseline plus a static CI gate that fails on growth beyond a declared threshold, following the sdk-surface-snapshot precedent.

pm health --check-only currently emits 132,585 B (~33k tokens) and is the diagnostic AGENTS.md routes agents to; the instrument that would have flagged it on the introducing commit exists and runs nowhere.

message: Wire the token ratchet: it verifies the three known output-size regressions, was discovered from the closed baseline chore whose harness it activates, and relates to the diagnostic-budget task.
